articles.title: India's first audited skincare intelligence platform goes live
articles.content: August 24, 2026 | Monday | News Skin Beyond Borders (SkinBB) has announced the public launch of India's first independently audited, dermatologist-driven skincare ecosystem and marketplace. This integrated Skin Intelligence Ecosystem combines AI-powered technology, dermatologist-led expertise, and scientific product curation to help consumers make informed skincare decisions based on evidence rather than trends. Built specifically for Indian skin, climate, and consumer needs, the platform combines multiple proprietary technologies into a single ecosystem designed to simplify skincare while improving confidence in every decision. Most skincare marketplaces list what brands submit. Claims like "dermatologist-tested" or "clinically proven" accompany the product to the point of sale, leaving the consumer without a way to verify them. The marketplace itself has had no mechanism either. SkinBB inverts that sequence. Every product listed on the platform is reviewed through its independent Product Review and Advisory Council (PRAC) before it becomes available. The council evaluates products for ingredient safety, label compliance, and claim integrity. Only products that meet the standard are listed. VyBIE, SkinBB's Living Skin Intelligence engine, combines an individual's skin profile with hyperlocal environmental conditions, including UV radiation, air quality, temperature, and humidity, to generate contextual skincare guidance. VyBIE provides tailored skincare insights based on users' locations and environmental factors, translating complex data into practical guidance. Supporting this experience is the Skin Friendliness Index (SFI), a proprietary model for environmental skin health score that integrates UV exposure, air quality, temperature, and humidity into a single indicator reflecting how favourable the surrounding environment is for skin health. The platform also features LabelLooker, SkinBB's ingredient analyser, which helps consumers understand product ingredients, their functions, and whether they are suitable for their individual skin profile. Complementing this is Ingredipedia, the platform's scientific ingredient database, co-developed with VES College of Pharmacy (VESCOP), Mumbai, providing evidence-based information to encourage informed product choices. SkinBB further strengthens credibility through a Verified Dermatologist Network, where dermatologists are verified against the National Medical Commission (NMC) registry and their credentials are displayed transparently.

articles.title: National Space Day on August 23 - Manorama Yearbook
articles.content: • India celebrates National Space Day on August 23. • It commemorates the day when the Vikram Lander of Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully touched down on the Moon’s south polar region on August 23, 2023. • Chandrayaan-3’s landing point on the Moon is named ‘Shiv Shakti’. Private investment in India’s space sector • India is expanding its capabilities across launch systems, satellites, space applications and human spaceflight. • India’s space economy is valued at $9 billion as of August 2026. It is projected to reach $40-45 billion over the next decade. • India’s global partnerships reinforce its growing space leadership, with over 300 space cooperation agreements across 61 countries and five multilateral organisations, covering research, technology, joint missions and capacity building. • India opened its space sector to private participation in 2020, enabling industry and startups across satellites, launch systems and space applications. This marked a major shift towards a broader national space ecosystem. • Private investment in India’s space sector surged nearly six-fold, climbing from $100.5 million in 2021-22 to $618.5 million by March 31, 2026, with $187 million recorded during 2026 alone. • At present, there are around 440 space startups in India. • The Indian Space Policy 2023 further expanded private participation across the space value chain. • It also defined the roles and responsibilities of NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) and Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe). • NSIL, the commercial arm of ISRO, provides launch, satellite and space-based services and transfers ISRO technologies to Indian industry. • IN-SPACe enables private space activities through a single-window mechanism. • Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) rules in February 2024 were liberalised for the space sector. Up to 74 per cent FDI is permitted automatically for satellite manufacturing and operations, 49 per cent for launch vehicles and spaceports, and 100 per cent for satellite and ground-segment components. • Targeted financing is strengthening India’s private space ecosystem. The IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme supports early-stage space startups, the Rs 1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund provides growth capital, and the Rs 500 crore Technology Adoption Fund enables wider deployment of space technologies. India’s key future space missions • India is entering a new phase of human spaceflight, deep-space exploration and advanced space infrastructure. • The Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme was approved in January 2019. Its scope was expanded and revised in September 2024 to a total outlay of Rs 20,193 crore encompassing eight total missions, including precursor flights for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS-01). • It aims to launch a crew of three Indian astronauts to a 400-km orbit for a three-day mission. • The first uncrewed experimental mission to validate various technologies including Vyommitra half-humanoid is targeted in 2026. The crewed mission is targeted by 2027. • India’s planned five-module space station Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) is targeted for operationalisation by 2035, with BAS-01 planned for launch by 2028. • It will support long-duration human spaceflight, microgravity research and advanced space operations. • Venus Orbiter Mission is targeted for launch in March...

articles.title: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan launches India's first non-GMO popcorn maize hybrid seed
articles.content: News On AIR | August 24, 2026 1:35 PM Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan launches India’s first non-GMO popcorn maize hybrid seed Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has described the development of India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed as a significant step towards self-reliance in agriculture and strengthening the country’s home-grown innovation. Launching the seed at the Gourmet Popcornica facility in Musunuru, Eluru district, Andhra Pradesh, today, the Vice President said India had for years depended on imported hybrid seed technology for high-quality popcorn maize. He said the new indigenous seed would help end this dependence and open opportunities for India to export popcorn products to global markets. Mr. Radhakrishnan said the achievement reflected the entrepreneurial strength of Indian farmers and appreciated Gourmet Popcornica and its leader Pattabhi Rao for building a home-grown enterprise into one of Asia’s largest popcorn maize processors. He said more than 17,500 farmers in eight states, cultivating nearly 40,000 acres, are now part of the popcorn value chain. He particularly appreciated the fact that these farming families were undertaking cultivation without taking loans for the activity. Mr. Radhakrishnan appreciated Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s initiatives in agriculture and rural development. He expressed support for efforts to improve irrigation facilities across all districts and for the proposed linking of South Indian rivers. The Vice President said farmers are the backbone of the nation and stressed that agriculture must become more technology-driven, innovative and profitable. He highlighted the contribution of agriculture to the national economy and appreciated Central Government initiatives such as PM-KISAN, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, Kisan Credit Card and Namo Drone Didi. The Vice President said India, with its population of over 140 crore, cannot depend on imports for food security. He stressed that agriculture will continue to receive top priority and called for wider adoption of modern technology and innovation. He said every seed sown today should become a seed of a stronger, self-reliant and developed India tomorrow. The Vice President also felicitated farmers during the programme. Governor S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, State Ministers and officials were present.

articles.title: PM Modi Urges Private Space Sector To Build Global Aura Of Innovation As India ... - The Right News
articles.content: Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Telegram Viber Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged the private sector in space research to build a global aura of innovation so that people worldwide feel that if they want to make a career, they should go to India. Mr Modi stated this during an interaction with CEOs and founders of 20 space startups recently. According to the transcript of the interaction, which was released on National Space Day today, Prime Minister Modi also highlighted India’s cost-competitiveness in launching space ventures. During the interaction, Mr Modi urged the space sector startups to remain consistent in their efforts and build a robust space-sector ecosystem capable of attracting talent from across the world. During the interaction, Chief Executive Officer of India’s first space-tech unicorn, Skyroot Aerospace, Pawan Kumar Chandana thanked Mr Modi for opening up the space sector. He said that on 18th July, they successfully launched India’s first privately developed rocket. Meanwhile, National Space Day is being observed today. The country celebrates the day on 23rd of August every year to mark historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole, making India the first nation to reach the lunar south polar region. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended their greetings on the occasion. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan said, India’s remarkable achievements in space exploration stand as a testament to country’s scientific excellence, spirit of innovation and determination to push the frontiers of knowledge. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while sharing a video on social media, said that in the new global order, India is continuously expanding its space sector. On National Space Day, Union Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh said the historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 placed India among the world’s leading spacefaring nations and lauded the remarkable contribution of the Indian scientists. articles.title: KloudMate Unveils India's First Agentic Observability Platform with Auto-RCA and Self ...
articles.content: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], August 24: Unplanned downtime across cloud infrastructure, applications, and networks costs enterprises between $5,000 and $7,500 per minute; a significant financial hemorrhage according to industry benchmarks. For digital-first businesses, that figure compounds even faster, resulting in disrupted transactions, eroded customer trust, and engineering teams that are forever consumed by firefighting. AI-native Auto-RCA and Self-Healing Workflows compress incident resolution cycles by upto 50%, optimize operational expenditure, and reclaim engineering time lost to reactive firefighting. Bengaluru & Texas-based deeptech startup, KloudMate, today announced the launch of its Agentic Observability suite, an AI-native observability platform that detects, investigates, and autonomously resolves incidents, compressing resolution times from hours to seconds. The launch positions KloudMate among a select group of global technology providers pioneering agentic AI within enterprise-grade observability ecosystems, and marks a pivotal moment for India's fast evolving enterprise technology story. The suite introduces natural-language querying, Smart Alert Grouping, and Automated Root Cause Analysis (Auto-RCA) with Autonomous Triage, engineered to attack the two primary metrics that define operational economics: Mean-Time-to-Resolution (MTTR) and engineering productivity. In most early deployments, customers have seen MTTR drop by upto 50% and alert noise reduce by upto 70%, while significantly increasing monitoring their coverage. Extending this intelligence into action, KloudMate has also introduced 'Workflows', a visual, drag-and-drop orchestration engine that lets engineering teams design automated response playbooks for their infrastructure and applications. Workflows enables teams to pre-define deterministic sequences of remediation actions, such as restarting a service, scaling a resource, or rotating a credential, that execute automatically the moment a condition is met (or subject to engineer sign-off for critical workflows). Human judgment stays in the loop; the toil does not. A New Paradigm in Observability, SRE-Ops & Incident Management Traditionally, observability platforms have functioned as passive repositories of telemetry data, i.e. logs, metrics, and traces, that engineers must manually correlate during high-pressure outages. KloudMate's new suite reverses this paradigm entirely. The moment an anomaly is detected, the platform's AI infrastructure autonomously initiates an investigation, correlating disparate signals and surfacing a probable root cause before a human responder is even engaged. For enterprise leadership, this translates into a tangible shift: reliability stops being a cost-center that scales with headcount, and becomes an autonomous capability that scales with the business. In an environment where engineering talent is scarce and expensive, that is not a convenience. It is a competitive moat. Commenting on the launch, the founders of KloudMate, Amitava Saha, Bidyut Baruah and Pranab Buragohain unanimously echoed the same sentiments: "Observability was built to collect data. We built KloudMate to close incidents. For decades, the industry equated observability with data volume: more dashboards, more logs, more alerts, more noise. We have inverted that model. The minute an anomaly surfaces, KloudMate begins investigating, often before an engineer has even acknowledged the alert. This is not about replacing human involvement and judgment. It is about giving engineering teams a decisive headstart, backed by transparent, auditable evidence". A Milestone for Indian AI & Enterprise Tech. The announcement arrives at...

articles.title: Non-GMO Popcorn Maize Hybrid Seed: What Is It? C. P. Radhakrishnan to Launch India's First Seed
articles.content: Popcorn is one of the most popular snacks not only in India but worldwide also. Behind every bowl of popcorn, there are special varieties of maize grown. As per the PIB , on August 24, 2026, Vice President of India C. P. Radhakrishnan will visit Musunuru in the Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh. During his visit, he will attend a program held at the Gourmet Popcornica Factory, where he will launch India’s first Non-GMO High-Expansion Popcorn Maize Hybrid Seed. So, this is very important for students who are preparing for competitive exams like UOSC, SSC, Railways, or any state exams; these questions may be asked in these exams that what is a new popcorn maize seed? What does non-GMO mean, what is a hybrid seed, and why is it called high-expansion popcorn maize? Let’s understand all these basic questions in simple terms. Key Facts Aspects Facts What is being launched? India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed Who will launch it? Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan When? August 24, 2026 Where? Musunuru, Eluru district, Andhra Pradesh Venue Gourmet Popcornica Factory What type of seed is it? Non-GMO hybrid popcorn maize seed What does high-expansion mean? The popcorn kernels can expand well when heated Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan will visit Musunuru village in Eluru, Andhra Pradesh, today. ▪️He will launch India’s first non-Genetically Modified Organism (GMO) high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed in Musunuru. ▪️He will also felicitate farmers and address… pic.twitter.com/LtI0zcKFsw — All India Radio News (@airnewsalerts) August 24, 2026 What Is the New Non-GMO Popcorn Maize Seed? The new seed is a non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed. It is especially developed for growing high maize that can be used to make popcorn fro earring in snacks. It will be launched by VP C. P. Radhakrishnan , and it is India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed. It has three important features; these are: Non-GMO: It is not genetically modified through genetic engineering. Hybrid: It has been developed by just crossing selected parents, maize plants, to bring different and unique characteristics to these seeds. High Expansion: These maize kernels are expected to expand to a high degree on a larger scale when they convert into popcorn. So, these seeds were designed for growing a special type of popcorn maize rather than ordinary maize. What Is Popcorn Maize? Popcorn maize is a special type of maize whose kernels can pop when they are heated. A popcorn kernel contains a small amount of moisture inside a hard outer covering. When the kernel is heated, the water inside turns into steam, and while pressure builds inside the kernel, eventually the outer covering breaks open. The inside then turns into the familiar soft and fluffy popcorn. This is why not every type of maize can make good popcorn . Popcorn maize has special characteristics that allow it to pop properly. articles.title: India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 - GKToday
articles.content: Home India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 August 24, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India has approved the first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), a proposed Indian space station planned for completion by 2035. The station is designed as a low-Earth orbit platform and is linked to India’s human spaceflight programme under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Bharatiya Antariksh Station: Basic Features The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is planned as a 52-tonne space station in low-Earth orbit at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometres. The station is designed to support a crew of three to four astronauts for stays of three to six months. The proposed station will consist of five modules. BAS-01 and Design Development The first module of the station is known as BAS-01. The Baseline Design Review and System Engineering for BAS-01 were completed, and 31 baseline design documents were released. The Union Cabinet approved the development of BAS-01 by extending the scope of the Gaganyaan Programme. The estimated cost of developing and launching BAS-01 is ₹1,763 crore. The expenditure is planned over four years from 2025 to 2028. ISRO’s Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre issued an Expression of Interest to Indian industries for fabrication and realisation of the module’s physical structure. Gaganyaan Programme and Related Missions The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is part of India’s broader human spaceflight roadmap. ISRO has planned eight missions, including launch vehicles and satellites, and the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission is scheduled within the current year. Gaganyaan is India’s human spaceflight programme for sending astronauts into space. Important Facts for Exams The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is planned as India’s first space station. The station is designed for low-Earth orbit at 400 to 450 kilometres altitude. The proposed BAS will have five modules and a total mass of 52 tonnes. The Gaganyaan Programme is India’s human spaceflight programme under ISRO. Institutional and Parliamentary References The Lok Sabha received information on the BAS-01 module through written replies in 2025 and 2026. The National Level Review Committee finalised and approved the overall structural configuration of the BAS on 3 December 2025. The project is associated with ISRO, the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, and the Union government’s space policy framework. articles.title: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi
articles.content: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi The Hans India Update: 2026-08-24 03:14 IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi poses during an interaction session with the CEOs and founders of space startups on the National Space Day in New Delhi on Sunday New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday called for policy consistency and a globally competitive ecosystem as he interacted with chief executives of Indian space startups, saying India should aspire to become a destination where talent from across the world comes to build its future. The Prime Minister lauded the entrepreneurs for taking risks in a relatively new sector and for placing their faith in the government following the opening up of India’s space industry to private participation. He said predictable and stable policymaking was crucial to encouraging innovation and giving entrepreneurs the confidence to pursue ambitious ventures. “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” Modi said, stressing that those taking risks should feel assured of a supportive policy environment even when they encounter setbacks. The interaction covered a wide range of technologies and ambitions, including launch vehicles, satellite propulsion, orbital services, space debris removal, in-orbit refuelling, ground station networks and pharmaceutical manufacturing in space. A Skyroot representative described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and spoke about the July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. Calling the achievement only a “warm-up”, the CEO said it marked the beginning of the company’s larger journey. The company plans to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year and has already set up three factories with the capacity to manufacture one rocket a month, the CEO said. Its longer-term ambition is to scale up to one launch a week and eventually several launches a day. Modi also sought to know whether the successful launch had improved investor confidence and opened up new opportunities for the country’s emerging private space sector. Startup leaders said investor confidence had increased, while another CEO said the company had secured eight launch contracts in the past month, most of them from international customers. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” Modi observed. The Prime Minister also highlighted the opportunity to make India a major global hub for space talent. He noted that Indian professionals based in the US and Europe were increasingly seeking to return home and join Indian companies after the sector was opened to greater private participation. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” Modi said, adding that people should see India as a destination for building careers in the space sector. articles.title: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 'Sher' rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi
articles.content: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” IRRPL CEO Major Gen Sharma said. Updated on: Aug 23, 2026, 23:12:56 IST By HT News Desk Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link India has manufactured and tested a prototype of the 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle, with army trials for the weapon to begin in September this year, Major General SK Sharma said on Sunday, while sharing a video of the test firing. Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said. (LinkedIn/ Maj Gen SK Sharma, AVSM, SM(Bar), VSM) The rifles are manufactured by the Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited, a joint-venture of the Indian Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), along with Concern Kalashnikov and Rosoboron export from Russia. Maj Gen S K Sharma, who is the CEO and managing director of IRRPL, said the testing of the prototype was “a moment of immense pride” for the company. He said this was not just “localisation of selected components”, but was a “true, end-to-end ‘100% genuine indigenisation’ of the rifle.” He said the prototype of the first 100 per cent indigenised vehicle had “successfully undergone firing, including burst firing”, adding that the initial results were “extremely encouraging.” “A proud moment for IRRPL, our partners (AWEIL & OSL) and MSMEs, and the entire Indian Defence Industry. This is Atmanirbhar Bharat in action!!” Major Gen Sharma said. Also Read | India imposes phased ban on import of 405 defence items to boost domestic production ‘IRRPL moving towards production rate of one AK-203 every 100 seconds’ Major Gen Sharma said that with the successful testing of the first prototype, IRRPL would now focus on producing the requisite number of 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifles for trials to the Indian Armed Forces in September, 2026. The IRRPL CEO said the company will be “moving towards a production rate of one AK-203 (Sher) every 100 seconds,” adding that there is “much more ahead.” Major Gen Sharma further said that IRRPL was also looking to prepone the delivery timeline of the approximately 6 lakh rifles that it has to supply to the Indian Army “by almost one year”. He credited the company's efforts towards “capacity enhancement, indigenisation and production optimisation” for the efficiency.
